title: Long noncoding RNA Malat1 protects against osteoporosis and bone metastasis

predicted_errors.error_location: Results section describing single-cell RNA-seq datasets (reference 38)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Reference 38 is used to support two unrelated claims: (1) 'the EO771 cell line, a cell line derived from a mouse mammary tumor on a C57BL/6 background38' (describing the origin of a mouse breast cancer cell line used for intratibial injection), and (2) 'GSE190772 with samples from two patients with breast cancer bone metastases38,43' (describing a human clinical single-cell RNA-seq dataset). These are clearly distinct sources (a mouse cell-line paper vs. a human clinical genomics dataset) that should not share the same citation number, indicating a citation misattribution/duplication error.

predicted_errors.error_location: Results, Fig. 1b, c description of osteoclast markers
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text states MGCs show elevated expression of osteoclast markers 'including NFATC1, CTSK, DCSTAMP, ATP6V0D2, ATP6V0E2, and ATP6V0A1.' The well-established osteoclast-specific vacuolar ATPase subunit reported in the literature is ATP6V0A3 (formerly TCIRG1/Atp6i), not ATP6V0A1, which is a ubiquitously expressed isoform (notably in neurons) and is not recognized as an osteoclast-specific marker. This appears to be a factual misidentification of the marker gene.

predicted_errors.error_location: Abstract and Results, description of Tead3
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper repeatedly describes Tead3 as 'a macrophage-osteoclast–specific Tead family member,' implying that Tead3 expression/function is restricted to this lineage. However, TEAD family transcription factors (including TEAD3) are broadly expressed across many tissue types (e.g., placenta, skeletal muscle) in established literature, and no data within the provided text substantiates a claim of lineage-restricted specificity for Tead3. This represents an overstated or unsupported specificity claim that is not backed by evidence presented in the paper excerpt.
